paragraphs.source_en: “Madam, this is a meal I have brought for myself. Pardon the liberty, but I shall eat it here.” So saying, Meitei made a very polite bow. Whether this gesture sprang from sincere courtesy or from joking, one could not tell. The master's wife seemed at a loss how to reply; she merely said lightly, “Please do,” and watched to see how Meitei would eat. Only then did the master take his eyes from the photograph of the nude beauty and say, “Look here, soba in this heat is bad for you.”

paragraphs.source_en: Meitei took the lid off the steamer and said, “Oh, it will be all right. Things one likes seldom do one any harm.” He put a great deal of wasabi into the dipping sauce and stirred it furiously, saying, “Freshly made soba is a blessing. Soba that has gone limp is like a spineless, slack sort of man; I have never had any use for it.” The master warned him anxiously, “My dear fellow, with that much wasabi in it, won't it be too hot?” Meitei said, “Soba is something one eats with sauce and wasabi together. I suppose you dislike soba.” The master replied, “As for me, I like udon best.” “Udon is what horse drivers eat. There is nothing so pitiable as a man who cannot appreciate the taste of soba!” As he spoke, Meitei thrust in his cedar chopsticks and lifted up as much soba as he could, about two inches high. “Madam, you should know that there are many schools of soba-eating. Novices always try to soak it in as much sauce as possible and then chew and chew in their mouths. That way one cannot taste soba at all. It must be done like this: with one scoop, you hook up the whole lot...” Saying this, he raised his chopsticks, and the long strands hung neatly in the air more than a foot high. Mr. Meitei thought he had lifted nearly all of it, but when he looked down, twelve or thirteen tails of noodles were still clinging sentimentally to the bottom of the steamer. Still addressing the master's wife, Meitei said, “This fellow is truly long, isn't it, madam?” The master's wife answered in a tone of great admiration, “It certainly is long.” “You dip one third of this long fellow in the sauce, then swallow it in a single breath. You must not chew. If you chew, the flavor of the soba is lost. Its value lies in its slipping smoothly down the throat.” So saying, he raised the soba high with his chopsticks, and at last the soba left the steamer; he moved the chopsticks over the bowl of sauce in his left hand, caught the noodles with the bowl, and lowered the chopsticks little by little, so that the lower ends gradually soaked in the sauce. According to Archimedes' principle, the more soba entered, the more the sauce in the bowl rose. But the bowl had already been filled eight-tenths full with sauce, and before even a quarter of the soba on Meitei's chopsticks had gone in, the bowl was full. Meitei's chopsticks stopped about half a foot above the bowl and remained there motionless for quite some time. Naturally they did not move; if he lowered them even a little more, the sauce would overflow. At this point Meitei showed some hesitation, but he soon brought his mouth forward; after a slurping sound and one or two forced movements of his throat, the soba held in the chopsticks vanished at once. Looking again, one saw what seemed to be one or two drops of tears flowing from the corners of Meitei's eyes down his cheeks. Whether the wasabi had taken effect, or whether swallowing the noodles whole had been such hard work, remains unclear.

paragraphs.source_zh: 迷亭打开笼屉的盖儿，说道：“不要紧的，爱吃的东西，轻易不会对身体有害的。”他往蘸荞麦面条的作料里放进了好多芥末，拼命地搅动着，说道：“这新擀出来的荞麦面条就是好，荞麦面条若是放软了，和没有骨气的软瘫瘫的人是一样的，我从来就不欣赏。”主人担心似的提醒他说：“老兄，你放进那些芥末，不怕辣吗？”迷亭说道：“这荞麦面条就得蘸作料和芥末一起吃。你大概是不喜欢吃荞麦面条吧。”主人回答说：“我嘛，最喜欢热汤面。”“热汤面嘛，那是马伕们吃的。不懂得荞麦面条滋味的那种人简直是可怜虫！”迷亭一边说着，一边用杉木筷子尽量挑起好多的荞麦面条，足有二寸高。“太太，你可知道吃荞麦面条有多种吃法，那些刚学吃荞麦面条的生手，总想尽量多蘸作料，然后在嘴里嚼个不停，那样是吃不出荞麦面条的味道来的呀。必须是这样，一挑就得都挑起来……”他说着抬起筷子，那长长的面条整整齐齐挑在空中有一尺多高。迷亭先生以为差不多都挑起来了呢，往下一看，还有十二三根面条尾巴缠绵地没有离开笼屉底。迷亭还是以主人的妻子为对象说：“这家伙可真长哩，太太，你说呢？”主人的妻子用很钦佩的语气回答说：“真是长啊。”“要把这长面条的三分之一蘸上作料，然后一口气吞下去，不能嚼，一嚼荞麦面条的味道就没有了，必须是哧溜一下把它吞进喉咙里去，才算是够味哩。”说着他把荞麦面条用筷子高高挑起，荞麦面条这才离开笼屉，他把筷子挪向左手盛作料的碗上，用碗接着，一点一点把筷子往下落，面条的下端逐渐浸泡在作料里，根据阿基米德原理，荞麦面条浸泡进去多少，碗里的作料就增高多少。不过那碗里原装着八分满的作料，还没等迷亭筷子上的荞麦面条浸到四分之一，饭碗里的作料就已经满碗了。迷亭的筷子在离饭碗半尺高的地方就老半天一动不动了。筷子不动是理所当然的，筷子再稍许落下一点，作料就要溢出来了。此时，迷亭多少显出踟蹰的样子，但他很快就把嘴凑上前去，只听得哧溜一阵声响和喉头上下动了两动，筷子挑着的荞麦面条立刻就不见了。再一看，迷亭君的两眼似乎有一两滴泪珠似的东西，从眼角顺着腮边流了下来。是芥末辣得他如此呢，还是因为他费力地把荞麦面条整吞下去的缘故呢，这还弄不清楚。

paragraphs.source_en: The master said admiringly, “That is impressive. To think you could swallow so much in one go.” The master's wife too praised Meitei's skill at swallowing noodles and said, “That was really splendidly done.” Meitei said nothing. He laid down his chopsticks, struck his chest two or three times, and then said to the master's wife, “Madam, one tray of zaru soba should generally be finished in three and a half or four mouthfuls. If one cannot do that, one cannot be said to know how to eat it.” With that, he wiped his mouth with his handkerchief and took a breath.

paragraphs.source_en: Just then, for reasons best known to himself, Kangetsu made the effort to arrive in this fierce heat wearing a winter hat, both legs covered with dust. Meitei immediately said, “Ah, the handsome gentleman has arrived. I am in the middle of eating, so please excuse me.” Then, under the eyes of everyone present, Meitei shamelessly ate up the remaining tray of soba as well. This time he did not eat in the spectacular fashion he had used before, but neither did he repeat the unseemly performance of using his handkerchief and stopping midway for breath; in the end, he disposed of the two trays neatly and without trouble.
